summary: Use a stack: push every opening bracket, and for every closing bracket check that the top of the stack is its matching opener. At the end the stack must be empty.

blocks.title: Read the text and the pairs
blocks.text: `PAIR` maps each closer to the opener it needs, so one lookup checks any bracket type.

blocks.title: Empty stack, assume balanced
blocks.text: `stack` holds the brackets opened but not closed yet, in order. `ok` turns False at the first problem.

blocks.title: Opening bracket → push
blocks.text: Every `(`, `[` or `{` waits on the stack for its closer.

blocks.title: Closing bracket → must match the top
blocks.text: If the stack is empty, this closer has nothing to close (`)(` case). If the top is a different opener, the order is wrong (`([)]`). `not stack` is checked first, so `stack[-1]` never runs on an empty list.

blocks.title: Matched → pop
blocks.text: The pair is complete, so remove its opener. Other characters (letters, spaces, `+`) fall through both branches and are ignored.

blocks.title: Anything left open?
blocks.text: Leftover openers like in `((a+b)` were never closed, so the text is not balanced.

blocks.title: Print the result
blocks.text: Exact strings: `Result: Balanced` or `Result: Not Balanced`.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 10⁴ — each character is pushed and popped at most once.
pitfalls: Only counting brackets — `([)]` has equal counts but is not balanced.
Forgetting to check the stack is empty at the end.
